decision.summary: Landlord replied to the inspection email about an unapproved dog flap and a spare key after a lock change. The report confirms the flap, so our 'no issues' email was wrong. I corrected that with the landlord, asked the tenant about consent and the lock, requested a spare key, noted conflicts, set a follow-up and returned the ticket to auto.

answers.answer: Not yet. It becomes one if the flap or lock change turns out to be unauthorised and the landlord wants action.

args.body: Thank you for your email. First, a correction: our email of 17 Feb said no issues were found, but the attached inspection report does record two things: a dog flap installed in the back door (utility room), and sticker-type marks on the Bedroom 1 wall which the tenant is to remove and make good. Apologies for the confusion. On the dog flap, our records don't show your consent, so we are asking the tenant whether permission was given and will report back. On the lock change, our records don't show who changed it or when, so we are asking the tenant, and we are asking them to get a spare front door key to us by 25 Feb. Please tell us if you did consent to the flap or arranged the lock change yourself. We will update you by 22 Feb.

args.body: Hi, thanks for having us in for the inspection. Overall the flat was in good condition. Two things please: 1) The report notes a dog flap in the back door. Changes like this need the landlord's written consent under the tenancy's alterations clause (and pets clause). Did you get consent? If so, please send us a copy or tell us when and from whom. 2) Our records don't show a lock change on the front door. Was the lock changed, and if so who did it and when? Please get a spare front door key to our office by 25 Feb so we hold one. Also, please remove the sticker marks by the Bedroom 1 window and make good. Please reply by 22 Feb; we will update you then.
